title: Round 7, stream B: the nest's last guards walk round the lander to the hull (the cargo lag was a straggler tail, not the count), and the ARC-01's magnets stand dark until a wave rides the sled up the rail
context: The owner's notes 1 and 6 of 2026-11-05 (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-round-7-nine-notes-design.md, stream B). Note 1: 'a lag between clearing a nest and the cargo being available'; the design listed four hypotheses (dying bodies still alive, strays far from the site, queued guards held by the crowd gate, automated() false) and asked to measure first. Note 6: 'I insist' the launcher's side lights are NOT on at the beginning, they light up with the payload moving, 'the impression that it is a magnetically powered launch'.
decision: Note 1: no count rule changed (STORY_EXPEDITIONS.clearBelow 3 stays the owner's 'fewer than 3'); the guard walk is fixed. src/domain/guard-aggro.js hullField(adj, from, walkable, maxHops) gives the walking hops from the hull's cell over the floor a guard may stand on (no rock, nothing the base calls solid); guardExits takes it as `field` and, while the hull is within the nest's aggro reach, a guard takes the exits fewer hops from the hull, round the lander, falling back to the crow's exits off the field. src/fx/enemy-step.js guardField builds the field once per hull cell (out to the nest's aggro radius + 4 hops) when a guard asks. Harness: showcase.nest(id) (state, flag, carry, live guards with nest/hull distances, queued, reach, automated) and showcase.killGuards(id, cells, kind) (the old killGuards when called bare; td-tab's hook now delegates, killCreature handed to the showcase host); browser step --nest-lag (?lab=1 for the immortal hull: a 20 s watch, then the nearest guard within 3 cells killed every 0.3 s; asserts no guard beyond 3.5 cells after the watch, the pickup on the frame the count falls, the last ten within 6 s). Note 6: LAUNCHER_LIGHTS { magnets 16, ahead 2, trail 3, peak 2, breech 0.15, idle 0 }; src/domain/light-sequence.js lightsBySled(index, count, { ahead, trail }) replaces the round-3 lightLevels/sequenceSeconds (its test moved to the wave); src/fx/arc-launch.js magnetGlow(state): idle through the loading, only the breech up to 0.15 over the charge, the sled's own arcIndex the wave's head while it runs the rail, the last wave falling with the charge after the release, idle from release + 2 s; base-layout's launcher entry names `dark` meshes (PASSAGE_GATES, ACCELERATOR_LIGHTS) that story-base mount gives their own dark material copy, so the standing launcher is dark between launches; the per-magnet split now waits for a plain material and re-applies itself over whatever a print's skin puts back; arc-launch state() reports lit, glow (the materials' intensities) and split; --colony asserts the launch per frame.
outcome: Note 1, measured on rocket-a (hull parked at the site's stand, 55 guards, all spawned 2.4 s in, nothing queued, automated() true every frame, sector quiet or live alike): the flag, the state and the pickup all land on the frame the count falls under 3 (tPickup - tLastKill 0.02-0.03 s on every run, before and after). The lag is the tail: with a 2-cell kill reach the swarm was down to ten at 28.8 s and the last ten milled on the lander's flanks, dying one by one as they wandered into reach, the pickup at 68.4 s (a 39.6 s tail); with the field 25.0 -> 40.4 s (15.4 s). With the immortal hull and a 3-cell reach: base 5.7 -> 12.1 s (6.4 s tail), with the field 4.7 -> 7.1, 1.9 -> 4.4, 4.4 -> 6.9 s (2.4-2.5 s). Hypotheses a-d ruled out: killCreature sets alive false before the body deflates, no guard was queued (the crowd gate never holds guards; the Pearl pool had room), automated() never false on the route, no stray beyond 2 nest radii held the count. Note 6, --colony's first SOL-88 launch: before, the per-magnet split was undone by the ARC-01's print skin and all sixteen burned at once from the release (glow [[2],[2]] while the sled ran, a floor of 0.25 lit from the first frame, and after the first launch the gates' merged material kept 0.25 cyan for good); after, every magnet at 0 through the loading, the breech at most 0.15 over the charge, three full gates riding the sled's arc index from gate 0 to the exit over the 0.4 s run (two at the exit), the breech back under 0.3 behind it, all 0 from release + 2 s, the standing launcher's two meshes at 0 after the launch.
alternatives: A count rule in src/domain/expeditions.js (the brief's place for the fix): guards beyond 2 nest radii stop holding (design hypothesis b) would have changed nothing, the stragglers stood at 0.3-0.4 nest radii; queued guards counted only while their spawn is live (c) had nothing to act on. Overturned: the rule is in src/domain/guard-aggro.js, tested there.

Clear the nest at a share of its strength (fewer than max(3, 20 % of the nest) left: rocket-a at 10): cuts the tail to nothing but changes the owner's 'fewer than 3' and hands over the crate with ten guards round it; offered to the owner, not taken.

Light the magnets on a time sequence over the 0.4 s run (the round-3 step/ramp moved to start): reads the same at 60 fps but drifts from the sled when a frame hitches; the sled's own index is the payload moving.
Dim the standing launcher by editing the GLB's emissive: the pinned asset is shared with the terminal's bench and hash-pinned; a per-structure material copy keeps the asset untouched.
evidence: npm test (324 programs; test/guard-aggro.mjs gains the walk round a lander on a 3x3 patch, test/light-sequence.mjs the wave, the launch per phase and the dark entry), npm run check, npm run architecture (td-tab 5,349 lines, 0 net, 8 bytes fewer, no long line), test/host-contracts (78 factories).

Browser on port 18182 under the lock: --nest-lag probes before/after (scratch r7-base/nest-lag-*.json, nest-watch-*.json), --nest-lag PASS; --colony PASS with the launch-lights assertions (commit 0fdd269d; two runs red on the way: the split undone by the print skin, then fixed); --nest-guards red at nest-guards-blobs and --defense red at 'no unpiloted tower kill', both identical on 21eee83a itself (a base worktree run); the known base reds (--gunship, --grow, --story, --story-world) not run.

Open: the residual 2.5 s tail is the parked hull's shove (a guard that touches the hull is pushed back, so a stationary harness hull kills it on the second approach); a player ramming has none. The owner's eye on the wave: 0.4 s up sixteen gates is fast, a magnet's trail (3) is the knob.
